questions.prompt: What does this client do, for whom, and in which markets?
questions.why: Establish the business before discussing formats.

questions.prompt: Who is the day-to-day client contact and who can make decisions?
questions.why: Avoid unclear delegation and repeated approval requests.

questions.prompt: Which digital-marketing services are in scope, and which are excluded?
questions.why: Define the actual job and avoid unpriced work.

questions.prompt: What business outcome matters most, what is its baseline, and what would success look like?
questions.why: Connect content to a meaningful business result.

questions.prompt: What launch dates, seasonal events, milestones and dependencies matter?
questions.why: Make delivery and campaign planning realistic.

questions.prompt: What budget or time capacity is available for content, tools, production and promotion?
questions.why: Keep the plan feasible; record confidential figures privately.

questions.prompt: What deliverables, turnaround, revision limits and acceptance criteria were agreed?
questions.why: Make the service agreement operational.

questions.prompt: Who approves the onboarding brief and workspace?
questions.why: Name a real human for decisions the agent cannot make.

questions.prompt: What timezone, working days, meeting rhythm and response times should we use?
questions.why: Prevent scheduling and expectation errors.

questions.prompt: Who handles urgent incidents, corrections, complaints and approval delays?
questions.why: Give uncertain or urgent work a safe next step.

questions.prompt: Which company overview, onboarding deck, service agreement and business SOPs already exist?
questions.why: Reference current records before creating replacements.

questions.prompt: Who does what across leadership, sales, product, support, marketing, design and technical work?
questions.why: Build a delegation and handoff map.

questions.prompt: Where is the existing client/customer list and what profile fields can marketing access?
questions.why: Learn segments while respecting privacy and permissions.

questions.prompt: Which website, social accounts and listings are official, and who owns each?
questions.why: Prevent work on an abandoned or unofficial account.

questions.prompt: Which existing workflows or agencies already own this work? List their entry files or procedures if known.
questions.why: Bind the current owner rather than creating a competing process.

questions.prompt: What knowledge is undocumented, who can cover each role, and where do accepted changes get recorded?
questions.why: Make the workspace useful for another team member.

questions.prompt: Why does this business exist, beyond its products or services?
questions.why: Anchor the internal brand.

questions.prompt: What future is the business working toward, and which parts are aspirations?
questions.why: Keep future ambition separate from current capabilities.

questions.prompt: What does the business commit to doing now?
questions.why: Describe the present mission.

questions.prompt: Which values should shape behavior, and what evidence shows them?
questions.why: Keep values concrete without inventing outcomes.

questions.prompt: Who is the primary audience, buyer, user and decision maker?
questions.why: Choose whom the work serves; do not guess from an example.

questions.prompt: What situation makes them seek help, what job are they trying to finish, and what blocks it?
questions.why: Find recognizable buying triggers and useful content.

questions.prompt: What do we know from customer research, and which fears, beliefs or segments are still hypotheses?
questions.why: Separate researched evidence from assumptions.

questions.prompt: Who is a poor fit, and which markets, claims or use cases are out of scope?
questions.why: Avoid attracting the wrong demand.

questions.prompt: Which alternatives do customers consider, including doing nothing or doing it in-house?
questions.why: Frame competitive research without assuming weaknesses.

questions.prompt: What difference can the client prove, and what should the audience remember?
questions.why: Ground positioning in evidence.

questions.prompt: What personality or archetype fits the brand, and how should it behave?
questions.why: Translate character into writing choices without forcing a framework.

questions.prompt: How should the brand sound? Give accepted and rejected examples, terminology and style rules.
questions.why: Make voice reproducible.

questions.prompt: Which offer wording, core messages, promise, stories, name and tagline are already approved?
questions.why: Preserve actual approvals and leave undecided blocks open.

questions.prompt: Which phrases, comparisons, guarantees or claims need evidence or special review?
questions.why: Avoid making unapproved promises.

questions.prompt: Where are current logos, colors, fonts, photography rules, templates and asset rights?
questions.why: Use the right design files without inventing a visual identity.

questions.prompt: Which languages, reading level, accessibility and localization requirements apply?
questions.why: Make the content usable by the intended audience.

groups.title: Before, during and after the sale

questions.prompt: How do new prospects find the business, become engaged, and recognize a need?
questions.why: Describe discovery and acquisition without confusing traffic with demand.

questions.prompt: What action captures a lead or starts a purchase, and what value is offered?
questions.why: Connect discovery to the next useful step.

questions.prompt: What happens between first interest and purchase: follow-up, objections, nurture and handoffs?
questions.why: Plan support for real sales friction.

questions.prompt: What is the conversion path, who owns it, and what defines a qualified lead or sale?
questions.why: Define the actual commercial event.

questions.prompt: How are customers onboarded, supported, retained, expanded or invited to refer?
questions.why: Include customer experience, lifetime value and referrals.

questions.prompt: What content is needed at each step, what CTA fits, and what should never be pushed prematurely?
questions.why: Map content to the journey rather than copying one format everywhere.

questions.prompt: Where are demo, discovery or sales calls, interviews, support questions and loss reasons?
questions.why: Find the actual language and questions behind stronger content.

questions.prompt: Which customer profiles, use cases and buying-group details are current?
questions.why: Avoid mixing different audiences or prospect and customer states.

questions.prompt: Which case studies exist, what was the result, and where are the source and client approval?
questions.why: Keep exact evidence and publication consent connected.

questions.prompt: Which testimonials and one-line praises may be quoted, named or paraphrased, and under what permission?
questions.why: A proof format is not permission to invent or shorten a quote.

questions.prompt: Which metrics, before/after claims or screenshots have reproducible evidence and an approved time window?
questions.why: Do not combine unrelated results or turn estimates into outcomes.

questions.prompt: What proof is missing, who can supply it, and which public uses are blocked until then?
questions.why: Create an evidence request instead of filling gaps with plausible stories.

questions.prompt: Which VOC/customer-value themes, demo-call-flow, industry/news, competitor and coverage research libraries exist, and who owns their accepted outputs?
questions.why: Route to rich research and proof stores, not only a product-facts checker.

questions.prompt: Where is the record of backlinks, PR mentions, citations and peer shares, including date, exact URL, relevance, owner and any outreach limits?
questions.why: Observed links and mentions are evidence; a prospect list is not an earned placement.

questions.prompt: What products or services are being marketed, what do they do today, and what are their limitations?
questions.why: Works for products, services, local businesses and nonprofit programs.

questions.prompt: Who owns product/service truth, and where are current API docs when relevant, help center, FAQs, release notes and approved offer details?
questions.why: Marketing copy is a consumer of product truth, not its proof.

questions.prompt: How will we learn about releases, policy changes, discontinued offers, incidents or corrections?
questions.why: Prevent important business updates from remaining internal.

questions.prompt: Which online and sales surfaces need an update for each change, and who owns them?
questions.why: Track documentation, website, email, social, sales and existing content coverage.

questions.prompt: May prices, discounts, guarantees or competitor costs appear publicly? What approval is needed?
questions.why: Public pricing policies differ by client.

questions.prompt: What embargoes, launch readiness checks, rollback conditions or announcement sequence apply?
questions.why: An internal plan or feature flag is not proof of a released capability.

questions.prompt: Which channels are actually in scope? Use channel IDs from the list; an empty list means no channel production.
questions.why: Enable relevant branches rather than assuming every client needs every platform.

questions.prompt: For each selected channel, what audience, job, format, CTA and conversion does it serve?
questions.why: Give each platform a deliberate role.

questions.prompt: What cadence and production capacity are realistic, and who creates each asset?
questions.why: Avoid promising volume without people or inputs.

questions.prompt: Where are existing blog, newsletter, YouTube, LinkedIn and other selected-channel assets, inventories, editorial calendars and performance exports?
questions.why: Start from available material before making more.

questions.prompt: Which source assets may be repurposed, who owns the original, and which derivatives are required or optional?
questions.why: Preserve source identity and avoid duplicating ownership.

questions.prompt: Who reviews each selected channel for audience fit, factual accuracy and final acceptance, and what happens when a reviewer is missing?
questions.why: A new audience must reach the actual worker and reviewer; never silently fall back to an old persona.

questions.prompt: Which search intents, topic clusters, original expertise and existing pages should the blog support?
questions.why: Build an evidence-led editorial brief.

questions.prompt: Who owns research, drafting, CMS updates, technical SEO, site QA and publication?
questions.why: Preserve writing and technical ownership boundaries.

questions.prompt: Who subscribes, what recurring promise do they receive, and what evidence supports each edition?
questions.why: Define a publication rather than an email slot.

questions.prompt: Where are subscriber consent, suppression lists, sender setup, review and send authority documented?
questions.why: Keep audience permission and publishing authority explicit.

questions.prompt: Which video formats, presenters, footage rights, script review, editing, captions and thumbnails are needed?
questions.why: A script is not a finished or published video.

questions.prompt: Where are actual video URLs and native/exported views, retention, CTR and conversion data?
questions.why: Separate script delivery from platform performance.

questions.prompt: Is this a company page, executive profile or employee program, and who owns posting?
questions.why: Separate company and personal-brand authority.

questions.prompt: Which post formats and native performance exports will be tracked?
questions.why: A carousel PDF is not proof of a published post.

questions.prompt: Which social platforms, accounts, audience/community rules and content formats are in scope?
questions.why: Adapt to actual platforms rather than copying one schedule.

questions.prompt: Who handles DMs, comments, complaints, escalation and response times?
questions.why: Content production alone does not cover community management.

questions.prompt: Which ad platforms, budgets, agency responsibilities, approvals and spending caps apply?
questions.why: Do not infer spend or campaign-change authority.

questions.prompt: What are the offer, landing page, conversion event, tracking, creative tests and stop rules?
questions.why: Tie paid activity to a measurable and bounded experiment.

questions.prompt: Who owns website design, CMS, code, hosting and deployment, and what pages are protected?
questions.why: Prevent a content request from changing infrastructure.

questions.prompt: Which forms, booking paths, checkout flows, accessibility and mobile journeys need checking?
questions.why: Test the actual customer journey after authorized changes.

questions.prompt: What are the search, AI-answer and local-listing goals, baselines, query/page data and technical constraints?
questions.why: Separate discovery hypotheses from observed results.

questions.prompt: Who owns citations, backlinks, directories, PR and outreach, and what communication is authorized?
questions.why: Access to a contact list is not outreach permission.

questions.prompt: Which lifecycle or sales emails are in scope, what triggers them, and who owns consent and sending?
questions.why: Separate one-off copy from live automations.

questions.prompt: Which events, partnerships or PR programs need preparation, capture rights, follow-up and repurposing?
questions.why: Connect event activity to evidence and follow-up.

questions.prompt: Which business outcomes, leading indicators and quality measures will be reported?
questions.why: Separate traffic, engagement, qualified demand, sales and retention.

questions.prompt: Where are website analytics (for example GA4), search-console data (for example Google Search Console), CRM, sales-stage history and channel exports? Who owns definitions, access and refresh?
questions.why: Register actual sources rather than plausible connectors.

questions.prompt: How are conversions defined, deduplicated and attributed, and what cannot be proven?
questions.why: Do not claim content caused revenue from correlation alone.

questions.prompt: What reporting windows, baselines, lag and comparison rules apply?
questions.why: Avoid misleading period comparisons.

questions.prompt: How will sales and customer success report lead quality, objections, wins and losses?
questions.why: Close the loop from content to commercial learning.

questions.prompt: Who receives which report, how often, and what decision should follow?
questions.why: Make reporting useful rather than another dashboard.

questions.prompt: Which recurring status reports and private meeting briefs are required, for whom, with what privacy, source, owner and review gate?
questions.why: A sales/conversion dashboard does not replace a written client report or meeting brief.

questions.prompt: Define the metrics we will compare across channels, including units, denominators, attribution, timezone, windows, lag and source-specific limits.
questions.why: Views, opens, clicks, qualified leads and sales need explicit definitions before cross-channel study.

questions.prompt: What bounded cross-channel question should we study, for which dates and cohort, and which owner outputs can support it?
questions.why: Create a small cited evidence pack rather than searching every client file or copying a data warehouse.

questions.prompt: Where is the keyword bank, with query intent, audience, geography, volume/rank source, observed date and page/topic mapping?
questions.why: Keep measured query data separate from keyword ideas.

questions.prompt: Where is the ChatGPT/AI-answer prompt and answer bank, with exact prompt, model/product, run date, locale, answer, cited URLs and repeat-check rule?
questions.why: One model answer is an observation under stated conditions, not universal visibility.

questions.prompt: Which tools and accounts exist, what read/write scopes are granted, and where are manual alternatives?
questions.why: Installed tools and subscriptions do not prove access.

questions.prompt: How will secure invitations and credentials be handled outside this workspace?
questions.why: Never ask for passwords, API keys, cookies or tokens in chat or Git.

questions.prompt: Which data is confidential, restricted, consent-bound or subject to retention and deletion rules?
questions.why: Keep client and customer material inside its authorized private boundary.

questions.prompt: What may the assistant do locally, what needs review, and who alone can publish, send, spend or change production?
questions.why: Record desired delegation without granting it through the template.

questions.prompt: List the source files, documents, datasets and relevant public pages already available.
questions.why: Read supplied context first and ask only for missing information.

questions.prompt: Who maintains each source, how fresh must it be, and what is the evidence of its last successful refresh?
questions.why: A scheduled job or file timestamp is not a successful refresh.

questions.prompt: What is the source priority when files disagree, and which unresolved questions need an owner decision?
questions.why: Keep conflicts visible instead of choosing the convenient copy.

questions.prompt: Which claims, regulated topics, endorsements, licenses, accessibility or legal reviews require a specialist?
questions.why: Route actual requirements to an appropriate reviewer; do not invent jurisdictional advice.

questions.prompt: What one small, reversible task can prove the workspace and handoffs work before live integration?
questions.why: Separate setup checks from production reliability.

questions.prompt: Who maintains this workspace, reviews changes and receives the handover?
questions.why: Give maintenance and offboarding an owner.
